answer: Because the lagoon index resolves every citation against the saffron checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the umber audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 191 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 191 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 598 identities would post 2777 proofs and burn roughly 57 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
